utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon for the Prosecution, assisted today by Anna Svensson and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to the learned friends from the OTP, to everyone in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic, and Lana Deljkic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Before we call in the witness, the Trial Chamber would like to deliver an oral decision on one of the Prosecution motions. The Trial Chamber now renders its decision on Prosecution motion for leave to amend Exhibit 106. The motion was filed on the 25th of February, 2008, and the Defence response was on the 3rd of March, 2008. Exhibit 106 was admitted into evidence during the testimony of Witness PW-2 on 17th July 2007. It consists of the front page and page 25, page 24 in the English version, of a booklet entitled"Instructions to the Muslim Fighter, Zenica 1993." Page 25 contains the first two paragraphs of the chapter on prisoners of war. The Prosecution argues that due to an inadvertent omission, the third and final paragraph of such chapter was not included when it moved for the admission of the document into evidence. It now seeks for the amendment of Exhibit 106 to include page 26, which is page 25 in the English version, of the booklet. The Defence opposes the Prosecution motion, arguing that it was the clear and explicit intention of the Trial Chamber to admit only those two paragraphs. According to Rule 89(c) and (d), a Chamber has the discretion to admit: "Any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value," and to exclude any evidence "if its probative value is substantially outweighed by the need to ensure a fair trial." Furthermore, on the 24th of July, 2007, the Trial Chamber adopted guidelines on the admission and presentation of evidence and conduct of counsel in court. Paragraph 20 of those guidelines explicitly refers to the admission of lengthy documents, such as books, and requests each party "to specify which portions of the document it seeks to have admitted." The Trial Chamber recalls that during the hearing of the 17th July 2007, the Prosecution sought to admit the entire booklet "Instructions to the Muslim Fighter," after showing the front page to Witness PW-2. The Defence objected to the admission of such a lengthy document without its contents being commented on by the witness. The witness was therefore shown page 25 of the B/C/S version and was able to comment on the two paragraphs contained therein. The witness was familiar with the content of the first paragraph, but had no recollection at all with regard to the second paragraph. It is found at page 737 of the transcript, lines 22 to 25. When the Prosecution moved again for the admission into evidence of the entire booklet, the Defence objected, arguing that only those paragraphs on which the witness had commented should be admitted into evidence. The Prosecution heard no objections, and the Trial Chamber admitted into evidence only the pages that were shown to the witness. It is clear from the transcript that only the two paragraphs contained in page 25 of the B/C/S version were put to the witness, whereas no reference is made to the third and final paragraph, nor to page 26 of the B/C/S version, containing the third and final paragraph. The Trial Chamber finds that the Prosecution failed to the indicate on what grounds, rather than completion of the chapter on prisoners of war, the proposed additional paragraph should be admitted into evidence. The Trial Chamber therefore denies the Prosecution motion for leave to amend Exhibit 106, unless the paragraph in question is introduced through a witness. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence calls Witness Enver Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning to you, sir, and you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, I see you itching to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Adilovic. Could you state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Enver Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: What is your date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 10th of January, 1960, in the village of Kljaci, Travnik Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And are you working now? Are you in employment?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: My colleague's just pointed out your answer to my question about your ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: By ethnic group, what group are you a member of?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak, and I am a Muslim by religion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And before the war, what did you do for a living, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in Vitez --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the name of the company that you worked for in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Sintevit Company in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And what did you do for a living for that company?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber where you were living at the start of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I lived in Vitez, in the hamlet of Novaci.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when the war started in Bosnia and Herzegovina, did you take up any military duties?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: When the war started, I joined the Territorial Defence, and I was the leader of the platoon detachment there. That was the platoon of volunteers in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately when you became the leader of the platoon in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And did you remain in that position, as the leader of the platoon in Vitez, throughout the war, or did there come a time when that position changed?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed behind in the TO as the platoon commander until the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was set up, and then I joined the 7th Muslim Brigade on the 19th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you joined the 7th Muslim Brigade in November 1992, did you take up any position within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, I'll come on to that in a moment, but if I can ask you this: From April to November 1992, apart from working for the Territorial Defence in Vitez, did you work for any other military organisation?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can the witness please be shown Exhibit 104. I can indicate it's just the B/C/S version that I'm interested in. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's going to happen to us who are illiterate in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, you'll see that there's no need for us to see the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll look to you to lead us through.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see that document on the screen in front of you, Mr. Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can only see a document with some black marks on it, but I am not able to read any of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that what we can see there is a document with the heading "Muslimanske Snage" and then a list of names with numbers next to the names; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because I was never a member of the Muslim forces. I don't know who the members of the Muslim forces were, and I can't discuss this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could please turn to page 15 in this document, and the ERN number at the top of the page that we are looking for is 0603-2524. Here it is. If we can scroll down towards the bottom of this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see there an entry on this page at number 273? And there we can see a name "Enver ibn Sefik Adilovic."

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that, but I had never been a member of the Muslim forces, and in my view this document is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Have you ever at any time used the title "Enver ibn Sefik Adilovic" or have you ever been called by that title?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Never. I have never used the word "ibn," and I don't use it to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: What about the name "Sefik"; does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: A moment, please. "Sefik," father's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, let's just get it abundantly clear. The transcript says "father's name." Whose father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father. My father's name was Sefik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So during 1992, did you use or did you hear anyone else use or refer to each other by the title "ibn"?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody in my unit had that title, "ibn."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Insofar as this document with the heading "Muslimanske Snage" has what appears to be your name in it, it might be suggested that this document shows that you were a member of the Muslimanske Snage. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I told you my comment. I said that I had never been a member of the Muslim forces, and to my mind this document is null and void.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, there is an extension of the indication of the witness's -- or not the witness's, but the name under rubric 273, there's something that looks like an address. Can you explore whether the witness is familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see, after the words "Enver ibn Sefik Adilovic," there are some additional words? Do those words have any meaning to you?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Donja Dubravica, "bb." That was my pre-war address, and it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, does that satisfy your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, it certainly shows that the name there was meant to be the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, I'd like to go back to the 7th Muslim Brigade. Did you join any particular unit within that brigade in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I belonged to the 7th Muslim Brigade -- rather, the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade that was stationed in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you joined the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, did you take up any position within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And the company that you became the commander of, did it have any particular name, or number, or any other form of identification?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Right after it was set up, a Krajina company was also formed comprising people who had fled from Krajina, so it was called the Krajina Company. I don't recall the number that it bore, whether it was the 1st, the 2nd or the 3rd, but it didn't really matter to us. I was the commander of the Krajina or the Krajiska Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: As to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, can you tell us where the command of the brigade was based?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The command of the brigade was located in Travnik, right next to the police HQ. That's where the battalion command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, who was the commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade at that time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Fadil Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you a few more questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade. The 1st Battalion was based in Travnik. Where was the actual command of the whole brigade located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think there's cross-purposes discussion between you and the witness, Mr. Robson. You see, when you look at line 2 of page 10, you said: "As to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, can you tell us where the command of the brigade was?" I don't know why 1st Battalion was part of that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the answer gave you the command of the brigade, not of the battalion. And now you're asking again for the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You're right, it's my mistake, Your Honour. I apologise, and I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Adilovic, if I've confused things. You were a member of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Can you tell us where the Command of the 1st Battalion was?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The Command of the 1st Battalion was in Travnik. It was called "Nas Dom." Upstairs, that's where the command of the 1st Battalion was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And is that the place that you mentioned which was close to the police station?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, right next to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from the 1st Battalion, were there any other battalions within the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: There was the 2nd and the 3rd Battalions that were part of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And where was the 2nd Battalion located, if you know? And this is the command I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It was stationed in Zenica, Bilmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And the 3rd Battalion, can you tell us where its command was?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can. I can give you the municipality, and that's Kakanj, but I can't give you the name of the exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. And above the battalions, if I can ask you about the 7th Muslim Brigade Command. Do you know where the brigade command was located?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The brigade command was in Zenica at Bilmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So does that mean that the brigade command and the 2nd Battalion Command was located at the same place?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: In the same area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Turning to the zone of responsibility of the first battalion you were a member of, can you tell us where it was?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion was at Bijelo Bucje, which is at Turbe, close to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You say it's close to Travnik. Can you tell us approximately how far away Bijelo Bucje is away from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly, 10 to 12 kilometres. I can't be more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Have you heard of the villages of Mehurici and Maline?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I hail from the Bijeljina Valley and I know the area of Mehurici, Maline, and the general area there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, in which region of Bosnia and Herzegovina are those villages of Mehurici and Maline?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That's the Bijeljina area, the Biljanska area. As you turn -- before turning to Travnik, you go up there towards Rudnik, Han Bila, Mehurici, Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, do you know which municipality those villages are in?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Travnik Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Concerning the zones of responsibility of the three battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the 1st, 2nd and 3rd, did any battalion have a unit located or based in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, which was the closest battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade to the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that the zone of responsibility of the 1st Battalion was Bijelo Bucje. Were you engaged in combat there at all, that's you and your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was directly there in the defence in the event of an aggressor's attack on the village of Bucje, so I was in the defence. As for combat actions, no, I did not execute any.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you were there in the event of an aggressor's attack. Just so we are clear, which aggressor were you defending against whilst you were at Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was defending it from the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to say approximately how long the 1st Battalion was deployed at Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've told us that the 1st Battalion was deployed at Bijelo Bucje. Are you able to say approximately how long the battalion was deployed there?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, when the 7th Muslim Brigade was formed, we took over Bijelo Bucje, and then until the end of December I was there. Then I moved on. After, in 1993, again our area of responsibility was Bijelo Bucje once more. I can't really tell you this precisely, because I was there until April, then I moved to the other side, actually to a different place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, if I may just interrupt, there's something that I don't understand here. Sir, were you, while you were at Bijelo Bucje, defending against the Chetniks, were you ever engaged in battle with any unit of the Chetniks, defending yourselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was only conducting defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. My question to you is: In conducting your defence, were you engaged in battle, or what's meant by conducting defence? Let me ask the question: How did you defend your area against the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chetniks always tried to carry out attacks to capture the village of Bucje, and so on and so forth, those areas down there, and we, when they attacked, would carry out the defence. And naturally you had these combat actions. We put up resistance so that the Chetniks would not get into Bijelo Bucje and capture Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's better. So you were involved in combat, which is what you were saying you were not involved in a little earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not plan or have any actions that we would embark on an assault when I was in Bijelo Bucje, for us to attack the Chetniks or to take their positions and so on and so forth. Our task was to be on the defence, to keep what was ours, and to keep that from the Chetniks. The Chetniks were trying to capture the village of Bucje and Pulac and so on and other areas, but we rejected those attacks. So while I was there, there was no action on the part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina towards the Chetniks. We would try to repel their attacks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand perfectly what you are saying, sir. You did not launch any attacks against the Chetniks. You merely defended. But in defending, you do get involved in combat. This is all I wanted to clear. Thank you very much, Mr. Robson. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: While you were deployed at the lines at Bijelo Bucje, did you see any foreign fighters of Arabic or Turkish origin whilst you were at the lines?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: While I was on the lines in my unit, there were no foreign members. I didn't see them or encounter them anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that in December, you -- I think you said you left Bijelo Bucje. Could you explain for us what occurred in December? And just so we're clear, which year are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about December 1992, I was in the area of responsibility, and the period that I was supposed to stay at the area of responsibility had already expired, so I was waiting for relief so that I could go for a rest. In December 1992, in late 1992, our replacements came. I completed the shift. I pulled the people back from the lines, sent them to Travnik. I was the last one to leave. When I came to Travnik, to the battalion command, I was told that the police were going to take me to Zenica, to the brigade command, and that down there -- should I slow down -- that the unit of mine was there at the brigade command at Bilmiste, and that we should go towards Visoko. So I left Travnik to go to Zenica, and I got a different assignment in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. So if I can just ask you a couple of questions about that. So you've told us that you pulled back from the lines at Bijelo Bucje to Travnik, and there you were told that your unit was at the brigade command at Bilmiste; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: My unit, when we left Bijelo Bucje and came to Travnik, was immediately told to continue in the vehicles to the brigade command in Zenica. That's where it was located, and that's where they were billeted, down there. So they did not have the rest that was planned for them. They straightaway continued for the Bilmiste barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then you told us that you left Travnik and you went to Zenica, and there you got a different assignment. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you did, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us about that new assignment that you were given? What was it?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: When I came to Zenica, I met Asim Koricic, Serif Patkovic, Ramo Durmis, and some other commanders at the brigade command, and they told me that we should go to Visoko with the units and that an action was being planned for the Visegrad feature. I was not quite happy for the soldiers of my unit to be sent from the ground into an action, in the belief that they first needed to rest, and then the planned engagement of my unit. Anyway, this is what happened. They proposed that I should not be the commander of the company in that action. They took my deputy, but they wanted me also to be there, to take part in it. And I was told to be a kind of operative in the field, to monitor the action, so that I could report to the forward command post of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So I'll just ask you a few questions about what you've just told us. You mentioned several names. Can I clarify, who is Asim who was Asim Koricic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Asim Koricic at the time, I think, was the chief of staff. I'm not sure, because the brigade had just been formed, so I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The chief of staff of which unit, just for the purposes of clarity?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The Command of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You mentioned a second name, Serif Patkovic. Do you know what position that person held at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then the third name you mentioned was Ramo Durmis. Do you know what position that person held at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the company in the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you told us that an action had been planned for the Visegrad feature in Visoko. For the benefit of those of us who do not know where Visoko is, could you tell us, from Travnik, which direction would you need to go to get to Visoko?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Travnik-Vitez-Kakanj-Visoko. That's how you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you had been the commander of the Krajina Company within the 1st Battalion, and when you got to Zenica and met with the commanders of the 7th Muslim Brigade, you were told that you were going to act as an operative during this combat action. Did you, in fact, perform the role as operative?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I did, but without any equipment. We didn't have -- I wasn't able to -- I had no electronic communications with the field, to the forward command post, so what could I do? All I could do was to have the right to use a courier from any company of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Before you tell us about that, I should ask you: Did the combat action at the Visegrad location actually take place? And this is in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know the date or the approximate date when the action took place?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The 28th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, who did those combat activities take place against?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know how long the action lasted for on the 28th of December, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: About 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And so can you briefly tell us what you actually did when you acted as an operative during the action? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was just monitoring the units when they arrived in front of the Chetnik lines and as they broke through the lines and captured the lines and advanced. When the lines were broken of the Chetniks, when the units began to move, then there was some kind of self-willed advance into the depth, and I was not able to control each individual in each unit. It started from persons -- I was able to follow as one person what was going on only for one place, so I could only see those that were closest to me. I wasn't able to monitor all of them. So I would send out a messenger to stop a little bit to see where we would go, what would happen next. So it was my duty also to inform the forward command post about what was happening in the theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So there was a forward command post. Could you tell us, where was that forward command post located in relation to where the action was taking place?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Behind our back. That was actually where the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was holding its lines. I don't know what the exact feature was. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know whether there are any commanders of the 7th Muslim Brigade at that forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Asim Potic [as interpreted] and Serif Patkovic were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry, could I just clarify the first name you mentioned? You said "Asim." Could you repeat the surname, please?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In acting as an operative and monitoring the combat operations that day, did you see any foreign fighters of Arabic or Turkish origin at the place where the combat was occurring?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Did you see any foreign fighters at all that day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That day, when I was going towards the command post, the forward command post - it's called Crni Potok - I saw -- since I was going to bring the men to carry away the wounded and the dead, one platoon, I saw a couple of them, four or five foreign members, but I didn't have any contact with them, I couldn't speak with them, and I don't know how they happened to be there. This was behind our back, behind Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Earlier on today, you mentioned the person called Ramo Durmis, and you told us he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt? Is the witness able to tell us of what origin these four or five foreign fighters may have been, if he knows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In terms of their appearances, are you able to say did they look of African or Asian or European origin?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I wasn't really paying attention, but I could see they were of a darker complexion. I saw hair. I mean, I didn't really speak with them. I couldn't talk with them. I just passed by. I didn't ask them anything, they didn't ask me anything. I don't know if they were able -- I didn't know if they were able to speak Bosnian, if they were saying anything or not. I had my task, my direction of where I was going, and I had my own problem to solve, and that's where I was going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How did you determine that they were foreign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only by their darker complexion. Maybe I could be making a mistake, but in my opinion, since I know how Bosnians look, judging by their appearance, I could tell that they were foreign members by their complexion. I couldn't say if they were black. They weren't too dark. I don't know what they were. They weren't even wearing uniforms, uniforms of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to remember what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was cold, so they were wearing these long coats. I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was their colour the only criterion that you used or was there anything else you observed on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, only the colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, going back to Ramo Durmis that you mentioned a little earlier, did you see that man during the combat action at Visoko?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was this combat in Visoko or was it in Visegrad? Earlier, this transcript said "Visegrad."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Why is Visoko being mentioned? Visoko is being mentioned because this is the Municipality of Visoko. The action was carried out at the Visegrad feature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. You see, some of us don't know the geography, so if we keep changing names, we get lost. So if you say "Visegrad," stay with "Visegrad." If you have to change over to "Visoko," say, "Visegrad, in the Municipality of Visoko." We don't know the geography, sir, so please don't be impatient with us. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if I can just clarify one final point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The elevation Visegrad, which municipality was that in?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it's in the Municipality of Visoko, because it's immediately above Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, I don't know whether you answered my question. Did you see Ramo Durmis during the course of the combat action that day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know, after the combat action that took place at Visegrad elevation, did you ever see Ramo Durmis again?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: After the 28th of December, 1992, I personally never saw Ramo Durmis again, to this day, until now. I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: At that stage, he was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Is there any reason why you didn't see him again after the combat action that day?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a reason, there is a reason. I don't know what his reasons were. He was making problems of some sort, so I don't know all the details, but according to my information he was no longer even a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I never saw him. I don't even know if he's alive today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The information that you had, do you have any idea when he left the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't really tell you precisely, but it was sometime in late February or early May 1993. I heard this from others. I never saw him or spoke with him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then, finally --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Late February or early March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: About the combat action that took place at Visegrad elevation, what can you tell us about it? Was it a successful operation or what?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can only say that it was an unsuccessful action.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And what are your reasons for saying that, briefly?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can say that that was because we had many losses, a lot of wounded, and that's why it was an unsuccessful action. We didn't capture territory, we didn't keep the territory, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And after the action, what did you do next? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That evening, you mean? You mean that evening on the 28th of December, that day, where?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I mean rather more generally, after the conclusion of your participation in the combat action. What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the Krajina Company --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the first part of his answer?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: ... up until, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreter has asked you if you could repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: After that action, I stayed a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade, of the 1st Battalion, where I was company commander. And I was the company commander still of the Krajina Company up until March or April, early April. And then I was transferred. I received an order to transfer to the Vitez Company. And at that time, I was the commander of the Vitez Company. This is the 4th Vitez Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you remained a company commander of the Krajina Company up until March or early April of which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then you became the commander of the 4th Vitez Company?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In which battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was that company?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So during this time period, March and April of 1993, do you remember where the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was deployed?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It was deployed in the Bijelo Bucje, the area of responsibility of Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I'd like to show Exhibit 108 to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see that document in front of you, and if so, can you tell us briefly what it is that you see?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could close in on the bottom half of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to see who this document is from?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It is signed by the deputy commander, Asim Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can go up to the top half of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we look at point 2(a), do you see that, Mr. Adilovic, it refers to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we enlarge the English a little bit, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you read, Mr. Adilovic, that it refers to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade having around 325 soldiers engaged in Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about the bottom of paragraph (b). So if you look down from 2(a), you can see point (b), and in the last sentence of that paragraph, the document states in this paragraph: "Additionally, there are around 60 Arabs and Turks who are also not included in this total." So the document is talking about quantities of men. To your knowledge, in March 1993, were there 60 Arabs and Turks in the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were there around 60 Arabs or Turks that fought alongside the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade at Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document can be put away, and I'd like to show the witness Exhibit 995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see the document in front of you on the left-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can close in again on the signature at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, there's no name on this document, but do you recognise this signature at all?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recognize either the signature or the stamp even.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could return to the entire document, yes, please, and if we can close in on the top half of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So what we can see, Mr. Adilovic, is that this document is dated the 2nd of April, 1993, and it has a heading: "Warning." If we look at the first paragraph, do you see that there's reference there to various incidents that have been carried out by members of HVO units? Do you see the reference to various incidents?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then if we look at the next paragraph down, do you see that that paragraph refers to those incidents being -- what it says, "being done to foreign nationals, volunteers in our ranks, particularly those from Arab countries"? Do you see where the document says that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I do, but I'm also asserting that among our ranks there were no foreign members. I can't really comment upon this document, because it's invalid. In my company, in my unit and in my battalion -- or the entire 7th Muslim Brigade didn't have a single foreign member.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adilovic. Your Honours, this document can be put away. If we could please bring up Exhibit 996.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Adilovic, we can see that this is a document with the -- that bears the heading: "Bulletin," and it's from the Staff of the Supreme Command Security Administration. I suspect I know the answer, but did you ever see this type of document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: What I'd like to ask you about is some information that's contained in the first paragraph of this document, so the next one in both the English and B/C/S versions. Just before the B/C/S page disappears - it's gone - but I wonder if we could just quickly go back to ascertain the date of this bulletin. Do we see that the date of the bulletin is the 4th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So if we can go to the first half or the top half of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If you can briefly have a look at the information contained in the top half of this page, Mr. Adilovic. Would you agree that here we can see once again there's a reference to an incident that's being carried out?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. This refers to foreign members, but I'm telling you that there were no foreign members in the 7th Muslim Brigade. I don't know anything about these events, who captured who, where, and took them where. I don't know that. What I do stand by and tell you with certainty, that in my 7th Muslim Brigade there were no foreign members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, I think it would be useful if you could clarify with the witness just how he knows this. Did he have a chance to visit all the other battalions? I mean, I accept that in his own battalion, there would be no foreigners, but how could he know whether there were foreigners in some of the other battalions who were billeted elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll explore that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, you've told us that the commands of the 2nd and 3rd Battalions were in Zenica and Kakanj respectively. On what basis can you tell us that there were no foreign fighters within the battalions of the 2nd and -- within the 2nd and 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, on the following basis: When we were conducting combat activities, the 1st, 2nd and the 3rd Battalions, on the basis of that I was able to know that there weren't any foreign members in the 7th Muslim Brigade. I could tell by their looks, by their gait, by their behaviour, and I would have recognised them had there been any in any other battalions. And of course as company commander, I cooperated with the company commanders of both the 2nd and 3rd Battalions. And when I was a battalion commander, I cooperated with them. That was one team. We were one team. That was our community, and we had to know who was part of that in order to be able to know who we could cooperate with and rely upon. And of course I knew that there weren't any foreign members.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify that a little, you say you cooperated with the company commanders of both the 2nd and 3rd Battalions. During 1992 and 1993, what degree of contact did you have with members of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Listen, if my AOR was Bijelo Bucje, of course the 2nd Battalion arrived there, had their replacements there. They held some of the -- parts of the line there, and so did the 3rd Battalion. We rotated. If we were planning actions in different directions, we held briefings which included all the company commanders, battalion commanders, and the brigade commander, who was the one holding briefings. The brigade commander called and summoned all the company commanders. Even platoon commanders were present at the briefings, of course, and the battalion commanders, that the briefings were called by the brigade commander, commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And we briefed him on the problems we had in our respective units, and it was on that basis that I knew who was in the different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adilovic. Your Honours, I'm looking at the time, and I'm wondering whether this would be an appropriate stage to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it is convenient for you [microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you were saying that the foreigners were commanders of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion, I would like to know precisely which operations, which combat operations, and when you had operations together with the 2nd and 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: My fellow Judge, I think, said that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that since it was not said that foreigners were commanding the 2nd and 3rd Battalion, I would like to know which were the operations you conducted with the 2nd and 3rd Battalion and on what date, at what date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You spoke about the briefings, briefings with the commanders, but it wasn't said that the 2nd or 3rd Battalion were commanded by or headed by foreigners. Therefore, the only possibility for you to meet or not to meet those foreigners would have been during combat operations, concretely speaking. So I would like to know precisely when you were fighting on the ground with the 2nd and 3rd Battalion and at what date. That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the entire 7th Muslim Brigade is concerned and their activities, well, the different battalions went different -- to different places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not able to guide, because what I heard from the interpreter was French. So I don't know what's happening, so I don't know whether you may or may not proceed. Judge, will you please help us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I can hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the entire 7th Muslim Brigade is concerned, in 1993 it was towards Kiseljak, Fojnica and so on and so forth that all three of the battalions were engaged, the entire brigade was engaged. The entire 7th Muslim Brigade was also engaged toward Kiseljak, and in that brigade all the commanders were Bosniaks, all the soldiers were Bosniaks. There wasn't a single foreigner as a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade, nor did foreigners take a part in actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're speaking of which month in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't specify. I believe it was already the month of July and August. At any rate, in the second half of 1993. It was in that period that the brigade went everywhere at their full strength. It was only that at some point the 1st Battalion of the 3rd [as interpreted] Muslim Brigade was given the order to go to Igman, and I was part of that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the date that he mentioned concerning Igman?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, you are asked to repeat the date you mentioned concerning Igman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The month of August of 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take a -- is it convenient? We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The document on our screens can be put away, and I'd ask that Mr. Adilovic be shown document D913. If we could close in on the top half of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see that this is a document dated the 4th of March, 1993, which has the head be "Assessment of units for their use in combat according to the order of the 3rd Corps Command"? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can just go to the last page in both versions to see who it's from. If we can focus on the name and signature there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see who sent this document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Ahmed Zubaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know what position he held in March 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the top of the first page in both documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see that this document is sent to the chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, in the first paragraph, which has -- it's point (a). It states: "The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade numbers about 460 men and is carrying out defence combat operations in the sector of Bijelo Bucje." This document, which is from March, I think you said earlier in your evidence that you were carrying out operations in Bijelo Bucje at that time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The second sentence then says: "The battalion is composed of a unit of the strength of 118 men from Vitez who, for the most part, will not return to Travnik to the organic composition of the battalion." In March 1993, had you become the commander of the Vitez Company?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If you can have a look at this paragraph, please, would you agree or disagree that the information contained in the paragraph reflects the situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 1, it's the paragraph which has next to the little (a), the first one you can see on the page, and if you could read the whole paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, you may have heard it, but it's not recorded. The answer to your question: "If you can have a look at this paragraph, please, can you agree or disagree that the information contained in the paragraph reflects the situation at the time?" Do you know what the answer was? Can the witness please answer again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's reading the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, as far as the head count is concerned and the arrival of the units of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, this is accurate. The unit was partly in Bucje, partly at Rostovo, and of course it's only natural that it was in Gornji Vakuf as well as in Vitez, because there was a unit there which I later on took over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So does the document accurately show where the units of the 1st Battalion were in March of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And the places that you mentioned and the places that we can see mentioned in this paragraph, are any of these places in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In connection with this document, I'd like to ask you something else. And if we can look at page 2 of both the English and Bosnian versions. What I'm interested in, Mr. Adilovic, is the last paragraph, and I'll read out the relevant part to you. In this document, what we can see is it says: "Bearing in mind all that has been said, I propose: Halt activities on the Visoko battlefield until it is possible for us to leave the zone of responsibility in Bijelo Bucje and until the mountain and the city guerrilla groups come back from training." Where this document refers to guerrilla groups coming back from training, does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It does. This is the guerrilla group which was part of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, who were trained for combat in urban areas, that's to say in towns, in the streets, and for combat in the mountains. That was a unit of the 2nd Battalion, headed by one Senad Senci, that's how we called him, and they were part of our 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And so you've said this is the guerrilla group which was part of the 2nd Battalion. Is that the title by which this group was called,"the guerrilla group," or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us, do you know what the ethnic composition was of the members of this guerrilla group within the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: They were all Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, were there any foreigners within that group at all, particularly any foreigners of Turkish origin?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In connection with what you've just told us, Mr. Adilovic, I'd like -- First of all, Your Honours, could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In connection with this document, I'd like Mr. Adilovic to be shown Exhibit 319.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, can you see the document in front of you, which at the very top of the page says the words: "Personal participation in a task in the operation on 28th December 1992 in the area of Visoko: Place, Visegrad - hill 744"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we have the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll come to that in a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see the document, Mr. Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could please go to the bottom of page 2 in the English version and page 3 in the Bosnian. And, Your Honours, here we can see the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do we see here that the document has a name here "Selim Sisman."

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know who Selim Sisman is?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He was a company commander of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can return back to the first page in both documents, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So this document, which speaks of the operation on the 28th of December, 1992, in the area of Visoko, is that the same combat action that you described to us earlier in your evidence or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It's the same combat action, 28th of December, 1992, in which elements of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade took part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, during that action, can you tell us which battalions from the 7th Muslim Brigade participated?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st and 2nd Battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And what I'm interested in is in the middle of the English page, and in the Bosnian version it's a part which is -- it is the part which is just above the last paragraph. I'll read it out to you. Do you see where it says: "The Gerila reported for the first time at 0615 hours, and I found out that the attack would take place soon, as it did at 0630 hours. Senci led the Gerila, and after the penetration, I was supposed to link up with them." Do you see that part of the document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to explain at all what this part of the document means?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Since Senci was the commander of the Gerila, he was a member of that same unit. This means that the Gerila commander was in touch with the company commander. Senci led the Gerila, who were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, who were Bosniaks and members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, a little earlier in your evidence you referred to the guerrilla group which was part of the 2nd Battalion, and you said that that group was led by a man called Senad, and I'm afraid his surname has disappeared from my screen now. And in this letter -- in this document, we can see the name "Senci" is used. Are you able to explain why there are two different names?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It's like this: His name is Senad. We called him "Senci." It's a term of endearment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So that's like a nickname, or is it a nickname?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a nickname. We really liked him a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So the Senci who led the Gerila and who is referred to in this document before us, that's the same man called Senad who was the leader of the guerrilla group within the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that what you are explaining to us?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: On this document -- Your Honours, if we could please look at the second page in English, and it's the second page in the B/C/S version as well. I'd like to ask a question or two. If we can go to the top of the page in the English version, and if we can scroll down the page in the Bosnian version, please. Mr. Adilovic, if you can look at the paragraph which sits above Item Number 2, which says "Accomplishment of Task," what I'm going to do is read out a part of that paragraph to you. In the document, the author states: "I heard on the radio that Visegrad had also fallen and that the Travnik people were advancing fast with the Arabs down towards the Gerila, where they linked up." First of all, you were monitoring the combat operations that day. Did you see the guerrilla group of the 2nd Battalion participate in the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I linked up with the guerrilla group. They entered the Chetniks' depth a bit earlier, so I had to link up with them, that was my assignment, so that they wouldn't be left behind in the back. So I did link up with Senci's group. Yes, that's the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And this part of the document, which says that Travnik people were advancing fast with Arabs down towards the Gerila, when you observed the battle, did you see any Arab fighters or foreign fighters of Arabic origin fighting alongside the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the 1st Battalion is concerned, the Travnik Battalion, there were no foreigners in the combat actions. I clearly said where and when; that is, in the afternoon hours I saw a couple of people. I don't know if they were Arabs or not. I know that they were foreigners. And then this man that found out through the radio something, actually he couldn't have had the opportunity, and I know that, to be able to see exactly. I don't know what radio, how he did it. I don't know anything about this statement of his. But it's true that the 1st Battalion was advancing quickly, and they were advancing quickly, and I asked them to stop a little bit for us to get our bearings, not to go too far into the depth, not to fall into a trap. As for foreign participants, and it says here "Arabs," there were no such participants in my units on that day, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If I can just clear something up. When you said, "and then this man found out through radio something," who were you talking about when you referred to "this man"?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Battalion company who wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you're talking about the author of this document, Selim Sisman?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document can be put away. I want to return to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just get something clear. You say, sir, you linked up with this guerrilla group because they penetrated and you couldn't leave them behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I need to explain a little bit. The guerrilla group had a specific task, in the course of the night, to pass through the lines of the Chetniks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. Just listen to my question and try to answer my question. Did I understand you correctly to say that you later linked up with this guerrilla group because you had to make sure that they are not left alone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And according to this document, this is the same group that also linked up with the Arabs later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It linked up with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, I said "according to this document." According to this document, Travnik people were advancing fast with the Arabs down towards the Gerila, where they linked up. Now, there was only one guerrilla group, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One guerrilla group, and this guerrilla group led by Senci, who were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that's the group you linked up with later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, I now want to ask you about the time period following your appointment as commander of the Vitez Company, which I think you said was the 4th Company. Now, did anything happen during the month of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, why did I transfer, is that what you mean, as the commander of the Vitez Company?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No. The question is -- I'm trying to focus your attention on the events that occurred after you became the commander of the Vitez Company, and what I'd like to ask you about is whether anything occurred during the month of April of 1993.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this happened in the Vitez Company, because they started to refuse orders, or the company commander, who was Redzo Kavazovic at the time, they had a lot of problems about that to get to the area of responsibility of Bijelo Bucje and so on and so forth. And then as far as I know, Asim Bektas took over that company, and even then they couldn't and they didn't want to carry out the assignment to go to the area of responsibility in Bijelo Bucje. This is what I wanted to say. And then, finally, they had a talk with me, because I am from Vitez, I know those people, if I could then become the commander of the Vitez Company to get that company in order, in line, if I were able to work with it, and to see if they would carry out the assignments that I issued to them or that my superior command issued to me to issue them. So this is how I became the commander of that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So at a point in time, you were asked to get the Vitez Company in order, and then you became the commander of the company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, can you tell us again approximately when that took place?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: April 1993, I think. I'm not sure. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And once you became the commander of the Vitez Company, what happened next? Where were you deployed to?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The first assignment I got with the Vitez Company was to go to the area of responsibility in Bijelo Bucje, and of course I got the unit together in Vitez, I got them to the Travnik barracks or to the religious school, the Medresa. It was just on the eve of the Army Day in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Army Day celebrated on the 15th of April. So the plan was to stay until the next day, the 15th of April --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just so -- just to give you some explanation, today is Friday, and I'm trying to move quite quickly so that we can get through your evidence, with the possibility of you returning home this weekend. So I know that you have a lot to tell us, but I'd be very grateful if perhaps you could listen to the question carefully and give us a focused answer. So the question was: You told us you were deployed somewhere. Did anything happen during the course of that month, in April, briefly?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: There was an attack on Ahmici by the HVO in 1993, the 15th or the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And where were you at that time when the attack took place?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was in Travnik, with the unit, at the Medresa barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And what was the impact, if any, of the attack being launched in Ahmici; what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Since I did have the order for the area of responsibility in Bijelo Bucje and the entire company was from Vitez, and their families were there, and I was from Vitez, from Novaci and my family is there, then I asked not to go to the Bijelo Bucje area of responsibility but to go back to Poculica so that we could see what was up with our families. The war or the conflict with the HVO had already started that had attacked Ahmici in Novaci, and that day I called everyone together. And ultimately the roads were cut off, and I did set off towards Poculica with my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You set off for Poculica. You told us that you were from Vitez, from Novaci. Where is Poculica in relation to Novaci?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Novaci are at the very entrance to Vitez. Poculica is between Zenica and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you travelled to Poculica, which I understand from your last answer is past Vitez. How long did you stay in that area, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed until the roads were reopened again from Poculica to Travnik. This was sometime in July, I think. I'm not sure if it's -- if it was at the end of June and beginning of July. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, the end of June and beginning of July of which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And whilst you were in this area, the area around Poculica, did you remain in contact with the 1st Battalion Command in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, because the roads were not open anymore, so I couldn't stay in contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when the roads reopened either at the end of July or the beginning of -- sorry, at the end of June or the beginning of July, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Poculica during that time, but I was in touch with the Zenica Brigade Command, and I reported to the brigade command in Zenica immediately, and the brigade commander gave me an order to be resubordinated to the 325th, and that's where my area of responsibility was, at Poculica, at Sljivovica, and I held that when the road thing happened, and then I received an order from the brigade commander to return to the battalion command, and that's when I returned to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 325th what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 325th Mountain Brigade, Vitez Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that you returned to Travnik, to the 1st Battalion Command, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: July -- end of June, beginning of July, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, the time that you had been away from Travnik, in the Poculica area, do you know did units of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade remain in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Bijelo Bucje, in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you were -- as I understand your evidence, you were away from Travnik from the period of April until the end of June or early July. Were you able to ascertain what the units of the 1st Battalion had been doing during that time period?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was not in a position to know for as long as I was at Poculica. I couldn't know where they were. They were left behind me in the area of responsibility of Bijelo Bucje at the Medresa. I didn't know anything about them until I came to Travnik with my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you came to Travnik with your unit, did you find out anything then?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Then I found out about the participation of Juka's Company, that it took part in the Hajderove Njive action was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Hajderove Njive is in relation to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Hajderove Njive is immediately above our barracks near Travnik, thereabouts, above our barracks maybe some 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know, did you find out had any units of the 7th Muslim Brigade been involved in combat activity in the Bila Valley region during that time period?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If I could show the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand that answer, in relation to the question, "I didn't."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If I could clarify, Mr. Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Did you hear any information or did anybody tell you that units of the 7th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The question seems to be leading the witness to an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, you gave us an answer before. Could you just clarify what you meant by that? You said, in response to my question, you said: "No, I didn't."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And maybe to help the witness, Mr. Robson, if you can use one verb. You see, in response -- when he gave that answer, you said, "Do you know," "Did you find out?" You made two questions. Similarly, just before the objection, you said, "Did you hear any information or did anybody tell you?" Just put one question at a time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: What I'll do, Mr. Adilovic, is go back to the initial question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Did you find out whether any units of the 7th Muslim Brigade had been involved in combat activity in the Bila Valley region during the period that you were away?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't find that out. I don't know of any units participating in the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Please, could we bring up D807 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So we see here a document, Mr. Adilovic. Do you see that it has a date at the top of the 5th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can just go to the bottom of the page in the Bosnian version and page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you see whose name this document bears?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was just looking at the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
