utterances.text: Are we okay now, sir? THE REPORTER: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Adilovic, we have a document on the screen in front of you. I'd like to ask you some questions about it. We can see at the top of the page, it has the title "Extraordinary Combat Report." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see that in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree that the document bears the name "Nenad Alagic"?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I would, yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can go to the top of the page, we can see there's some information under the title "Aggressor," and at point 1(b), which is the second paragraph, it says: "HVO units units ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And at the bottom of that second paragraph, in section 1(b), it states as follows about the HVO units: "Firing positions are as follows: Hajderove Njive ...," and it continues. Does that mean anything to you, where it says "firing positions at Hajderove Njive"?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The firing positions at Hajderove Njive were the HVO positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And those HVO firing positions, where were they aiming towards?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: They were aiming towards the town of Travnik. All around the town, there were HVO positions targeting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And further down the page, we can see section number 2, which has a heading "Our Forces," and I'm interested in the third bullet point down. So if we could go down in the B/C/S version. Do you see the bullet point that says: "1st Battalion, 7 Muslim Mountain Brigade is engaged on the direction towards Hajderove Njive, linking it to itself and covering with its MB (mortars)"?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that, and that's the information I received when I arrived in Travnik; namely, that this unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade was engaged along the axis of Hajderove Njive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could that document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1197.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 290.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, while we're waiting for the document to explain -- to appear on our screen, I can explain that this is a document from the same time period, June 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, as we go through these documents, as we are going through these documents, I would be grateful if you would be so kind as to explain to us the relevance of these, because it is simply unclear to me. And may I remind you that you have, I would expect, about 45 minutes left of your time, so if you would do us the favour to strengthen the Chamber's grasp of these -- of this examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll endeavour to do so, and I can also indicate that it shouldn't be too long left of this examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see in front of you a document which has the heading "PWO Milinfosum number 59," dated the 27th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't make this out really well. It's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, I don't expect you to have seen this document during the war, but I want to ask you some questions about the information in here. Can we please turn to page 2 in the English version, and it's page 2 in the Bosnian version as well. And if we can scroll down, please, to the bottom of the page, it's point number 10 that I'm interested in. So if you can just -- Your Honours, I see that there's a discrepancy between the English and B/C/S versions. You can see, in the English version, under "ORBATS" it has "Number 10", whereas in the B/C/S version under "ORBATS," it has "Number 7". I believe that's a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So what must we look at in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a Prosecution document, so we'll have to have this rectified in due course, but if you'll bear with me for the moment and we'll deal with the document as best that we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I'm asking is what should we look at, should we look at number 10 or number 7? Number 10 in the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Number 10 in the English, and it's 7 in the B/C/S at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll just read out to you what the document states, Mr. Adilovic. So it says that there was an ECMM report that Franjo Nakic, a deputy commander, OZ Central Bosnia, claimed that the 7th Muslim Brigade comprised of three subordinate battalions. He also added that they were fanatics, of which 10 per cent were foreigners, and who were used -- if we can just turn over onto the next page in English, please -- manoeuvre unit to reinforce main points of effort. My first question is: Do you know who Franjo Nakic is? Have you ever heard of that person?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we look at the information which is contained in this document, it states: "7th Muslim Brigade HQ Zenica." And then if we move down, it says: "1st Battalion, 7th Muslim Brigade, Travnik." We can then see under that: "Commander Asim Koricic." Was the commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade Asim Koricic in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Asim Koricic was never the commander of that battalion or any of the battalions of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we go down to the next part of the document, there is information about the companies of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. It states the companies Travnik, Mehurici -- sorry, Your Honours, it's the next page in the B/C/S version, if we can turn over into that. It states the companies are Travnik, Mehurici, Ravno Rostovo. Were those three locations places where the companies of the 1st Battalion were deployed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would submit that that is a leading question. Perhaps the witness could be asked to comment on what he sees, as opposed to asking whether he agrees -- whether he agrees whether those companies were deployed in those locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you have any comment at all about where the document speaks of the companies of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade being at Travnik, Mehurici and Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade never had a unit stationed at Mehurici or the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then finally on this document, there is a comment at the bottom which repeats what we saw on the other page, and that is that 10 per cent of the 7th Muslim Brigade are foreign nationals. Do you have any comment about that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It is 100 per cent certain that the 7th Muslim Brigade had, as its members, all Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know which ethnic group Franjo Nakic was a member of?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. This is the first time I hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Your Honours, this document can be put away. If we can please bring up document D49.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see a document in front of you dated the 19th of July, 1993, which states at the bottom that it's the commander of the 1st Battalion of the Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, here the commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade signed the document, Safet --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the second name, the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, Safet Junuzovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you recognise the signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can look at the heading, it states: "Response to request." In your evidence a moment ago, you said that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade never had a unit stationed at Mehurici or the Bila Valley. I'd like to ask you about this document, and in it we can see it says the following: "We are not able to grant your request from 5th of July, 1993, because, as we officially informed you on several occasions, those units do not belong to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and therefore we do not have the right to command the unit at Mehuric camp." Do you have any comment on this document from the commander of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: This is an accurate document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And by that, do I understand you to mean that it shows that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade did not command any unit at Mehuric camp?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, the question has already been answered, but again I would submit that this is a leading question. The conclusion is being put to the witness, and the witness is really -- all he's required to do is say "yes" or "no," and which he did and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was seeking to clarify the answer given earlier by the witness and my understanding of that answer, in which he said it was an accurate document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then if you want clarity, you say, "What do you mean by that?" That's how you put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to put that question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's superfluous.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I would ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to that. The document has effectively been read into the record, so I don't see any purpose in burdening the record any further by having this particular document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has confirmed that the document is from a person that he knows of. He recognises the signature, and he's confirmed that it is an accurate document. And Your Honours will be able to determine yourself whether it matches what he's been telling us during the course of his testimony. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Listen to the gravamen of the objection, sir. That's not the objection. You're not answering to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask that it be admitted into evidence so that we do have a copy of the actual document on the transcript. We can see here information which has not been read into the record. If we don't have the document admitted into the record, yes, we will have the evidence on the transcript, but it could cause difficulties to both parties and the Chamber if we don't have the actual document as a trial record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What difficulties?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the practice of this Chamber, we have occasions when lengthy parts of documents have been read out, and that has not precluded the documents from being admitted into evidence. As I say, without the document being admitted as an exhibit in the case, we stand every chance of losing sight of this evidence. As I say, there is additional information contained in the document which has not been read into the record. It's an important issue in the case, and I would suggest that it's in the interests of justice for the Trial Chamber to have this document so that it can use it at a later stage. And, of course, this is not a case where the author of the document is unknown to the witness. The witness has identified the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, as I understand the objection, it says the document has been read into the evidence in its entirety, the entire content of the document has been read into the transcript. That is the basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Your Honour, if I could make a further point, and perhaps it's the simplest point of all. You can see that I haven't read the entire document into the record. I only referred to the central paragraph and the author of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any reply, Mr. Menon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would just note for the record that the content of this document only contains one paragraph, and when I look at the transcript, it's clear that the witness has identified the author of the document, it's clear what the purpose of the document is, the title of the document, and the one paragraph, its entire content, the substance of the document is on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, your learned friend's response is that not the entire document has been read in. I guess he means, by that, that he didn't read the official stamp affixed, the Republic of Bosnia, and the whole address.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I would simply note that we're not contesting the authenticity of this document, so I really don't see what added benefit having the document on the record would really present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge Lattanzi has a question to put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Perhaps I missed something out. In any case, I don't understand, Witness, whether your company, after you had returned to Travnik, whether your company was still or was no longer part of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Perhaps I missed something out. I'm awfully sorry if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I returned from Poculica to Travnik with my unit, where I reported to the battalion command, and I remained part of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And I continued being a member of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, I have another difficulty with this document, and that is that my difficulty relates to the probative value. All the document says is that it confirms that the 7th Muslim Brigade -- or, rather, the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade did not have a unit at the Mehurici camp. Is that -- I need to see it more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can just briefly state the Defence position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It refers to a request number 01/700/2 from 5th July, because "as we officially informed you, those units do not belong to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade." That's what it says. And then in your question, which I agree was leading, you then had the witness confirm that this implied that there were no Muslim -- that no foreign -- let me see if I can find back to your question. You said: "Do I understand you to mean that it shows -- this document shows that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade did not command any unit at Mehurici camp?" What is the probative value of this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have to look at the indictment, and, obviously, the Prosecution's case. It's the Prosecution's case that foreign Mujahedin fighters were subordinated to and incorporated within the 7th Muslim Brigade. They also talk about a unit of Mujahedin at the camp. In the indictment, it talks of Poljanica, which we've heard is close to Mehuric, so here we have a document which speaks directly to that issue that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade did not have the right to command a unit at Mehuric camp, so that shows, in our submission, it's relevant to whether there were persons subordinated and incorporated within the 7th Muslim Brigade; it also is relevant to the issue whether they had the ability to control others based at that location, so we would say it's highly relevant. And if I might add something, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let us wait for the French translation. Very well. It seems to say that at least the 1st Battalion did not control anything in Mehurici. That may well be true, but does that speak to the fact that the 7th Muslim Brigade had no control over the activities in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously that's an issue that you're going to have to explore at a later stage, but it's been the Prosecution's case that it was the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, indeed that's the evidence that we've heard today, that operated in this part of Central Bosnia. So as to whether any of the other battalions could have had some control, that may well be an issue for you in due course, but we would say it's the 1st Battalion which is the relevant battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So what we see here is merely a confirmation of what the witness has already confirmed at several occasions during his testimony, that at least in the 1st Battalion there were no foreigners?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We would say it's documentary evidence which supports what you've heard from the witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, perhaps if I can just also say: Clearly you've heard the contents of the document, but in due course you will have to consider the weight to attach to documents -- of all documents that you've received as exhibits in the case, and my submission would be that without the original copy, without the markings it has, without being able to see stamps and signatures, that will be an extremely difficult task for you to decide what weight, if any, to give to this piece of evidence we have today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. If the Trial Chamber may just rule on the objection. I think this document is so brief that it hardly adds on to any burden that the Trial Chamber already has. The document will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become 1198.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time. We're past the normal break time, but I'm just wondering whether you'd like me to continue. I should be able to finish certainly within five minutes, or if you'd like us to take the break at this stage, we can do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: One of my colleagues on the Bench just whispered that we take the break. Court adjourned, and come back at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The final document I wish to show Mr. Adilovic is Exhibit 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, while we're waiting for this to appear in English, would you agree that we can see that this is a short document dated the 27th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you see the document, Mr. Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree that it has the date the 27th of May, 1993, and it bears the name "Asim Koricic" at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If I could quickly read to you the first sentence of the document, it states: "We are unable to obey point 6 of your order strictly confidential number 02/33-1281 of 27 May 1993 because we do not have insignia showing membership of the unit. We did not get these and so the process of marking has not even begun." And my question to you, Mr. Adilovic, is: Do you recall whether you and your subordinates had received insignia for your uniforms by the end of May 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't receive the insignia of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and when I was the battalion commander at the end of 1993, not even at that point did I have the insignia of the 3rd [as interpreted] Muslim Brigade. We had constant problems with these -- with the insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So just so I'm clear, even by the end of 1993, you and your subordinates had not received insignia of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade --

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adilovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Robson. Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Adilovic. My name is Aditya Menon, and I will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution. If my question -- if you don't understand my question, please make that clear, and I will try to restate it. My intention isn't to trick you. Let me begin by asking you -- confirming that you testified in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And that was on the 12th of April, 2005?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you answered the questions that were put to you truthfully?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Pardon? Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: When questions were put to you during the course of your testimony in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case, you answered those questions truthfully?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Truthfully, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And did you answer those questions fully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And wouldn't you agree with me that at the time that you testified in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case, which was in 2005, your recollection of the events in Central Bosnia in 1992 and 1993 were perhaps clearer at that time?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I only spoke in more extensive terms at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir. Let me begin by confirming that you joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in November 1992. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, upon the setting up of the 7th Muslim Brigade, which was in the month of November, I joined it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And at the time that you joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, you joined specifically the 1st Battalion of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And this battalion was based in Travnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And it was specifically headquartered in the Medresa building in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, the units, that's to say the soldiers, were billeted at the Medresa in Travnik. We called it "Medresa," but it was our barracks. The command of the battalion was billeted at our dom, close to the police station. So the commanders and assistant to the commanders were up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you do know that the Medresa building was used prior to -- prior to it having been used as a facility by the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, 1st Battalion, it was used by the Muslim Forces of Travnik? Can you confirm that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that, because at the time I wasn't there at all. I was at Visoko, at the Territorial Defence there out in the field. Who was there, reporting at the Medresa, I don't know about that. I was a member of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that, sir. Now, sir, when you joined the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, how many companies were there within this battalion?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It was planned by the establishment to have four companies. I don't know whether they were all formed at the same time. I took up the Krajina Company and went out in the field. The Ravni Company was also established, and the Vitez Company was set up at a later stage. The setting up -- or, rather, the establishment of the battalion envisaged four companies. I don't know whether they had full manpower levels. I don't think any of them were, except for perhaps the Vitez Company, and only at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But at the time that you joined the 1st Battalion, sir, can you tell me who the other company commanders were?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was a company commander. Ramo Durmis was a company commander, and the late Muharem Salkica was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, you say, and you restated this -- you restate the fact that you were a commander of the Krajina Company, and I want to refresh your recollection with what you -- with the statement that you had given during the course of your testimony in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case. And for the Court's benefit, this is at page 18313 of the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura transcript, and the line reference is lines 10 through 17. Sir, you were asked -- and I'm just going to read out the relevant part of that question: "I'm not entirely clear about the date you became a company commander. It must have been sometime in November, perhaps sometime later. Can you specify when it was that you became a company commander? I'm not talking about the Territorial Defence of Vitez. I'm talking about the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, that is." And your answer, sir, was: "I believe it was by the end of February 1993." And then later on, an additional question was put to you, sir, and again this is from the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case. And for the Court's benefit, this is page 18335 of the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura transcript, and the line references are 8 through 22. And the question, sir, was this: "Before you were appointed the commander of the company in February, you said that in November you had filed a written request to join the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade to Mr. Haso Ribo, and then you were -- in fact became a member of that brigade. In what capacity were you a member of the brigade between November and February? What were you doing? What sub-unit of the brigade were you attached to before you became the commander of the 2nd Company?" And, sir, your answer was: "Right. I was not carrying out any duties on the basis of any documents, orders, or anything like that. I was within the unit, within the battalion. I was following the situation of the units. That was my task until the setting-up order, gathering of the people from the battalion to form companies. So I followed the situation within the unit. I went to Bijelo Bucje, et cetera, and I said I went to Visoko. And I was simply following that action, nothing else, as a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade." Sir, do you recollect the answers that you gave and that I just read out?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that bit precisely, but I can give you an answer to it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: If you could do that, sir.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, the 7th Muslim Brigade that was set up according to the document on the 19th of November, 1992, and its units were not put together, all of them, so that you could say, "This is the unit of the brigade," or, "This is the 7th Muslim Brigade." It was only the start of the setting-up process. There were proposals at the time as to who should be the commander, the deputy commander, and so on and so forth. When you appoint a commander in writing, well, you can also appoint him orally first, and only later on will the document be made certifying his appointment. There was a war on. As soon as I reported to the 7th Muslim Brigade, I wasn't able to stay back home or to be idle within the brigade. I had to move around to set up the company. In fact, I myself set up the Krajina Company and became its commander. We were doing this as we went along, as the war was going on, and we were trying to create all the conditions that needed to be in place. Now, the follow-up documents, the underlying documents, came only at a later state -- stage. Initially, there were differences of opinion, and it wasn't possible to achieve such a high degree of organising in order to -- for the brigade to become immediately operational. You had some men who were resting at home, some were away. The 7th Muslim Brigade was indeed set up, but it was set up within a process that went hand in hand with the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get some clarity. When the follow-up documentation came, did it appoint you with retrospective effect to the date of the oral appointment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. Whatever I did, as soon as I joined the unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We haven't got much time. Just listen to the question, answer the question, and that's it. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the start of -- at the start of your testimony here, I had asked you whether you answered the questions in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case truthfully and fully. When the question was put to you as to when you became a company commander within the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, why didn't you at that time indicate that you were the company commander of the Krajina Company as of November 1992?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I've just answered this question. The forming of the brigade was underway, and I was assigned the Krajina Company. These people were not assembled. I went to Bijelo Bucje to assemble them, and time was passing. When the time was ripe and when we were all assembled, then I officially became the company commander. I know, based on my own documents -- I knew that I was the commander of the company, the Krajina Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: When did you officially become the company commander of the Krajina Company, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the moment, I cannot recall when that was, officially, but it was from the period of the establishment of the company. I was acting in the role of the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And I go back again to the answer that you had given in response to a question as to when you had become a company commander in the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. And you referred to the date of end of February 1993. Can you explain to us what the relevance of that particular date is, then, in light of the testimony that you've given here today?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: When I came to the 7th Muslim Brigade, I was sent to Bijelo Bucje, and in my opinion, I was the commander of the company. As for the information of the 7th Muslim Brigade, what that information is, I don't know. I don't know right now if we're talking about January, February, December. Please, I also went on the 28th of December in 1992 to the Visegrad feature. I came from Bijelo Bucje as company commander, and I stated that here. And in the Kubura case, you'll probably have the information that I handed over the company and became an operative on that day, on the 28th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Actually, sir, that's not particularly clear from the Kubura transcript, but that's not my point. My point is simply: An answer that you had given while testifying and an answer in relation to a question as to when you became a company commander, your answer was "at the end of February 1993." Now, that date hasn't come up in your testimony today, and I'm simply trying to reconcile the testimony you gave in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case with what you've said today, and I just simply want to know: What is the relevance of this date at the end of February 1993? Because that was your testimony, sir.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that testimony doesn't stand in relation to the Vitez Company, because as of January, late January and February, I was asked to take over the Vitez Company, so according to that testimony perhaps it says that I was the commander of the company at the time, the Vitez Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I'll move on. Sir, I want to ask you some questions in relation to the Visoko operation that took place at the end of December 1992 and about which you've testified this morning. Sir, do you know which other -- do you know which other units, other than the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, participated in that particular operation?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall that right now, but I think there were units from Visoko, but I don't know. I really cannot give you an answer, because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell me, sir, how that particular -- excuse me. Can you tell me, sir, how the attack on that day was organised?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: My unit was given the axis, where to enter, where to work. We were there from the Crni Potok toward the Chetnik. We broke through the lines. We got out there to the elevation. We secured it. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, on that day, were you participating in the combat?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That day, I was an operative monitoring the unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade or, rather, of the 1st Battalion. I was a coordinator on the ground, coordinating with the forward command post of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, just so that I'm clear, in relation to the combat activities, how far away were you from those activities?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I went with the fighters of the 1st Battalion directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Did you advance with those fighters?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But since the line was broken through and we were spreading to the left and the right, I could have gone to the left or the right, so I was going in one direction for an hour, then I would stop and change direction, and then do that again after an hour. I didn't have a set place where I could be there all the time and follow what was going on. I was moving from spot to spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, were you in contact with the company commanders who were leading the attack from the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And how were you in contact with them?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Physical contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell me who was in overall command of this particular operation?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, the 7th Muslim -- the 1st Battalion was commanded by Asim Koricic and Serif Patkovic, who were there at the forward command post. As for others, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay. So if I were to tell you that it was, in fact, Kadir Husic who was in charge, who was actually a member of the operations group Visoko, you wouldn't know that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't. I was responsible for my own unit, and I was also reporting to Asim Koricic and Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, did you participate in any of the reconnaissance that took place prior to that operation?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part in the reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And can you tell us what you did, exactly?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: We all went. The commanders, I went with them, including Asim Koricic and Serif Patkovic to reconnoiter the Chetnik terrain to see where we would go in and what we would do. This was reconnaissance from our lines, immediately if front of our lines, to see where the Visegrad feature was, how we would get in there, where the 1st, where the 2nd, where the 3rd would go, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, you were shown this morning a report that was prepared by Mr. Selim Sisman, and in that report he refers to the participation of Arabs in this particular operation, Arabs, foreigners, generally speaking, in this operation. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can bring up Exhibit 319, and if we could go to page 2 of the English version of this document. And if we could scroll down on the Bosnian version of this document. If we could go to page 2 of the Bosnian version of the document as well. If we could scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I would direct your attention to the middle portion of the document that you see. Do you see a reference there to the following statement: "I heard on the radio that Visegrad had also fallen and that the Travnik people were advancing fast with the Arabs down towards the Gerila, where they linked up, as I found out later"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I do see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: So you agree with me that Mr. Sisman is referring to the participation of Arabs, the presence of Arabs, during the course of these combat activities?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you explain why?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Because I was at Visegrad with the units directly, reconnaissance and all the preparations. During that time, there were no Arabs. The Gerila was there belonging to the 7th Muslim, and these were Bosniaks. So if he heard this over the radio, he couldn't have seen it himself. He might have heard something, somebody might have told him. So as far as I'm concerned, this item is inaccurate, especially because I was there myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you would -- if you would please listen to my question carefully, I'll restate it. My question was simply: Do you agree with me that Mr. Sisman is referring to the participation of Arabs, the presence of Arabs, not whether he saw them, whether he's stating that he saw them, but merely the fact that he's referring to the participation of Arabs? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may assist, the Prosecutor perhaps can specify what he means "there," because in that way the question is hard to understand in our language. Can he just explain what he means when he says "there," meaning the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, in this document, as I read it, Mr. Sisman is referring to the participation of Arabs at the operation in Visoko. He's saying that he heard on the radio that Visegrad had fallen and that the Travnik people were advancing fast with the Arabs down towards the Gerila, where they linked up. And I'm simply asking you to confirm whether this statement refers to the participation of Arabs in this particular operation at Visoko.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: There was no participation of Arabs at Visoko at the axis where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you about your personal recollection. I'm simply asking you what appears on this document.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if they took part at all, Arabs, in that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, sir, that's a different answer than what you had given us this morning, because this morning you had given us an affirmative answer, that they did not participate. Now you're telling us that you don't know if they participated.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: They did not participate. I said that this morning. Arabs did not participate at the Visegrad feature with the 7th Muslim Brigade unit, and that is something that I am confirming now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe, if I may just find out, sir, do you agree that this document on the screen relates to the Visegrad combat of the 28th of -- 28th of what, April?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: ... December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the document, it is said that it is the 28th of December, 1992, and that's the date when we were in this action. As for the participation of the units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just listen to my question. Answer the question and the question only. Then we'll move a little faster, and then you will go home and spend the weekend with your family, rather than stay here for the weekend and then come back on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown Exhibit 121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Menon --

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- I can't help seeing the witness's answer to your question, if you go up to -- it's just on the top of the screen at the moment -- to line number 6 of page 27. You asked the witness if there were participation of Arabs in this particular operation at Visoko, and the witness answered: "There was no participation of Arabs at Visoko at the axis where I was." So still there is, in my view, some sort of misperception. Is the witness talking about what he could see from the point where he was or is he talking about the overall operation at Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you understand the Judge's question?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: In the planning of the action, no Arabs at all were planned in the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand that. Mr. Adilovic, one thing is that the participation of Arabs was not included in the plans, perhaps, but the issue is if Arabs, in fact, took part in the action somewhere; maybe not where you were. And I am sure that you're truthful when you tell us that you never saw any Arabs, but there could have been Arabs taking part somewhere else in that operation. After all, it was a big operation. The front line was quite extended. And I'm asking the question because it appears as if, from the document, apparently another company commander heard over the radio that the Arabs had taken part, and this is strange. Why would he say this if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, he heard through the radio communications that there were people from Travnik and the Arabs breaking through fast, but I was leading the Travnik people and the Travnik unit and following them, monitoring them. There were no Arabs at all within the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. There were no Arabs. I don't know who he heard this from, in which radio communication. This is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would ask that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge, we're getting no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat that. I was saying to the witness that I have a question, and I would like him to answer it without making any additional comments. This is my question: You said that for the planning of the action, no Arabs had been included or planned to take part in it. When you plan, you plan the participation of units, not of single individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, during the planning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No comment. I just want to know whether you plan units or individuals. That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Units of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown Exhibit 121, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we zoom in a little bit on the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 of the English and page 2 of the Bosnian version of this document. Actually, if we could go back to page 1 for a second of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at the title of this particular document and the first sentence. Do you agree with me, sir --

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, sir, that this particular document relates to the operation in Visoko on the 28th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the date of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 of the Bosnian version and page 2 of the English version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you see a name at the bottom of this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see "Ramo Durmis."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, earlier today you referred to Mr. Durmis' participation in this operation. Would you agree that he did, in fact, participate in this operation?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: He participated in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And he participated in the operation as a company commander within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page of the Bosnian version of this document and scroll up on the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, I would direct your attention to the paragraph which reads: "Some Mujahids, including Arabs, moved towards the elevation 744 and without my order. Then they came down to the village and started torching." Do you see that paragraph, sir? It should be at the middle portion of the text.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, sir, that Mr. Durmis is also referring to the participation of Arabs in the operation in Visoko which took place on the 28th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: According to the document, the way he drafted it, it's as if Arabs were participating there, but not under his control. They were not under his control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: My question, sir, simply is whether Mr. Durmis is referring to the participation of Arabs in this operation. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, this document, because I didn't see them personally, is not fully valid. I cannot respond to this question. I didn't have any assignments relating to them. They were not with me. They were not with our units, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, that was not my question. My question is simply: What appears on the page in front of you? We've confirmed that this particular document relates to the Visoko operation, and then Mr. Durmis, who is a participant in that operation, is the author of this document, and I'm simply asking you to confirm that he's referring to the participation of Arabs in this operation.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm this. This is what he said, but I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Move on, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honour. If we could go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in the open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just have a moment to consult with Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you for that break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. With the technological assistance of Judge Lattanzi, I've got the exhibit on the screen. All I wanted to mention is that this document also mentions not only Arabs, but Turks as well, in the sentence reading: "However, the Arabs went even further to the right. Amir Heldzic [phoen] and his group returned before the mid-day, but Abu Tallah, deceased, with the Arabs and the Turks, remained deep on the right side." You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll put a question to the witness in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know who Abu Tallah is?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, sir, earlier today you testified about the brigade commander summoning all the commanders of the battalions within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and all the commanders within -- of the companies within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, the witness doesn't get translation. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be of assistance, could Mr. Menon slow down whilst putting questions, because the interpreters have trouble catching up with him and then the question, as it comes to the witness, is presented somewhat differently, and this creates confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic, because we don't hear that part of the translation. We are grateful for you to bring that to our notice. Mr. Menon, will you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will take my learned colleague's advice and I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, sir, earlier this morning you testified about the brigade commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade summoning all the commanders of the battalions, all the commanders of the companies, and all the commanders of the platoons for a meeting -- for meetings or briefings. Do you recall having said this, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, when, in 1993, were such meetings held?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But during which part of that year, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: This took place sometime in the month of September of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: So this was after the blockade between Travnik and Zenica had been lifted?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We, as company commanders, had had them before as well; not the platoon commanders, but the company commanders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, can you clarify that a little bit, sir. Where were these company commanders meetings held?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: At the brigade command at Bilmiste, in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And when were these meetings held, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date. It depended on the possibilities of reaching Zenica from Travnik. Whenever we were able to reach Zenica and whenever the commander needed to talk to us to have us brief him, we had such meetings. I can't tell you exactly. Later on, after the blockade of the roads was lifted, we had meetings in Zenica on several occasions, and then the commander discussed with us the situation in the brigade as a whole, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm simply referring to meetings in the first half of the year of 1993, sir, and my question simply is: Why would you be meeting with the brigade commander? Wouldn't it be your responsibility to meet with the battalion commander, as a company commander?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, we also reported to the battalion commanders. However, when the brigade commander summoned battalion commanders and company commanders to report to him, then all of us went there, even when the platoon commanders were invited. Whenever we were summoned, my battalion commander would go there, I would go there as the company commander sometime, even the platoon commanders would go, because when the brigade commander wanted us to report to him directly, then all of us would go; namely, battalion commanders, company commanders, even platoon commanders, to report about the situation in the units, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade when you were having such meetings, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Amir Kubura was the one who held most of the meetings with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And these meetings, these large meetings, just so that I'm clear, because it seems a little unclear in the transcript, these large meetings with all the battalion commanders and all the company commanders and all the platoon commanders, these meetings took place on or after September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: That was before the month of September. In the second half of 1993, when the Zenica-Travnik road was passable, when everybody was able to come from Travnik to Zenica, and also those from Kakanj, from the 3rd Battalion, were able to come, and that's when we were able to discuss our work plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay. And just so that I'm clear, sir, now, there are three battalions within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And there were between three to four companies within each -- within each battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It depended on the manpower levels, if we had enough men. The plans were to have at least three to four companies. Now, whether this was feasible or not is a different matter. People were getting killed and wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And within each company, sir, how many platoons would there be?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: By the establishment, there would be three platoons, the 1st, the 2nd and the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And so we're effectively talking about around 40 commanders meeting for a particular briefing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, one would have to sum up the companies and the platoon commanders. It would take me half an hour to get all the figures right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But a lot of people, nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: -- who were deployed in different parts within the -- within Central Bosnia, within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Which period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period when these meetings occurred. You gave me an indication that these meetings were taking place on or around June 1993, before June 1993. Maybe you can clarify that for me. When exactly were these large meetings taking place, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you a date. The problem is as follows: As soon as the roads made it possible for us to have all the three battalions together, it was decided that the 7th Muslim Brigade should continue being engaged in combat with all the three battalions. Up to that point, it had been pretty chaotic. One battalion would go to Bijelo Bucje, the other one would go somewhere else, the 3rd Battalion would go to yet a third location. So at this one meeting, the commander and all of us decided that whatever was the AOR of the 3rd -- of the 7th Muslim Brigade, that it should be the AOR of all the three battalions, and that wherever the 7th Muslim Brigade was engaged, all three battalions should be engaged. What happened was Igman was the next action, and it was decided that the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade should go there, and that's when I joined them. But for the rest, except for Igman, wherever the 7th Muslim Brigade had its AOR, all the three battalions were deployed. They were no longer sent into different areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that long explanation, sir. Can I conclude from that that prior to the blockade between Zenica and Travnik having been lifted, it was very unlikely that you would have participated in such meetings, these large meetings in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Before the blockade?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Before the blockade, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was: Before it was lifted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Before the blockade was lifted, sir. Yes, before the blockade between Travnik and Zenica was lifted, it would have been unlikely for you to have participated in such large meetings in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I participated in them only when the blockade between Zenica and Travnik was lifted and when we could travel along that road. It was only at that point that we took part in these briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much for that, sir. Sir, would you agree with me that the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and the other persons who were at the command level of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade were perhaps in a better position to assess what the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was doing and who was a part of that particular brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That question is a call for speculation, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Defence counsel showed this witness a number of documents -- a few documents that were authored by the commander, or at least signed by the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and the witness testified, and those documents referred to the participation of Arabs, and the witness said he knew nothing about those documents and that those documents were wrong. And I'm simply trying to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I maintain the objection, but at the very least I would suggest that we would need a time frame for the question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to give a time frame, Mr. Menon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Give the time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, in the first six to eight months of 1993, wouldn't you agree with me that the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and other people operating at the level of the brigade command would have been in a better position to assess who was a part of that command -- excuse me, who was a part of the brigade and what exactly the brigade was doing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. We were the ones who reported on our different activities to the brigade, telling them what we were doing and what our status was, and they, in turn, issued us with orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, sir, your answer was: "We were the ones who were reporting on different activities to the brigade ..." As I understand your testimony, in this time period, in the first six to eight months of 1993, you were a company commander. And so what I'm going to put to you is that perhaps there were other commanders within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade who were reporting things that you didn't know about.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I sent reports to the battalion commander, and he, in turn, sent them to the brigade commander. I don't think that information was withheld within the brigade that the battalion commander would withhold some information from us that we wouldn't know. I don't believe that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, you haven't answered my question. My question was simply that there were -- that there were other commanders, besides yourself, who were reporting things to their superiors that you would not have known about.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Why can't you answer that question, sir? Did you know everything that was going on within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I was best acquainted with the best -- with the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. I was pretty much familiar with the brigade as a whole, but of course I could not have followed everything that was going on, and I'm not able to give you the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, sir, I think you have given me the answer. You just said: "I was pretty much familiar with the brigade as a whole, but of course I could not have followed everything that was going on ..." And I was simply asking you whether there were things that you probably would not have known about.

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You don't know that there were what, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: Things that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, sir, that means that you would have to know everything that was going on within the battalion and the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: It is only natural that I would not have been -- well, I'm speaking generally. I knew whatever I heard at the briefings. I knew what I experienced on the field. Outside of the briefings and direct experience, of course I could not have been in every place at all times. I followed the command-and-control system, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Okay. And that was simply my question, sir, again, but I think you've answered it and I'm not going to put it to you again. If I could just have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do have a moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, Mr. Robson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, two short points, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, it was put to you that there were three statements that contradicted your testimony today. I'd like to show two of the things which have been suggested to be statements. The first is Exhibit 121, if we can quickly bring that up on the screen, please. And I'm only interested in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just mention that up here, our screen that is supposed to show us exhibits is not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can supply hard copies, if that would assist. Exhibit 121. This is it. If we can go to the last page in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, it was suggested that this was a statement. Is this document signed at all? Do you see a signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't see a signature, and I said that I don't -- in my view, this document is not valid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can look at page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which document is this, because I've got --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is E121 on the screen now. That's what you should have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't have you on the screen. Is that the document written by Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Then we are on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Is it possible to have the entire page on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic, do you see any stamp, or signature, or markings on this page?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Again -- this is page 2. Again, do you see any stamps or markings or official signs on this page?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We've studied the final page already. If I can look -- last point, if we can look at Exhibit 319, please, and this is the second document which was suggested to be a statement that contradicted your testimony. If we can go to page 1, please. Mr. Adilovic, we can see some handwritten markings in the top right-hand corner, but do you see any stamp or official mark on this page?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can look at page 2, again, do you see any sign -- any stamp or official markings?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Finally, if we can look at the last page of the document. Do you see any signature for this document, or official markings, or stamps?

utterances.speaker: ENVER ADILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are very fortunate, Mr. Adilovic, that you will be able to go home. This brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you very much for taking the time off your very busy schedule to come to testify at this Tribunal. You are now excused, and you may stand down. And please do travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess this would be a convenient time to take the break. The matter then stands adjourned to Tuesday, the 11th of March, at quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
